about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: 5020 Engineering Resource Group Incorporated
channels.legal_basis: ADEM AEPACS NPDES SSO Event Reporting Form v1.5: "Immediate notification shall be provided within 24 hours of becoming aware of the event. ... The follow-up report shall be submitted within five days"; Ala. Admin. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.; NPDES permit AL0084498
channels.note: 5020 Engineering Resource Group Incorporated reports each notifiable sanitary sewer overflow to ADEM within 24 hours and files the 5-day follow-up through AEPACS; ADEM posts the report on its SSO map and layer within minutes, read by the al-adem-sso-history feed. None of its permits has a report on ADEM's layer (read 2026-11-07). The rule binds every NPDES permittee, public or private.

channels.name: 5020 Engineering Resource Group Incorporated
channels.legal_basis: Ala. Admin. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)
channels.note: No web form: the rule requires the permittee to report a notifiable overflow to the public as soon as possible but sets no channel or content, so no public page of the operator's is required; the operator's own pages were not searched one by one. The 2017 petition asking for a minimum standard was not adopted. The rule binds every NPDES permittee, public or private.

channels.name: Alabama Department of Environmental Management (Coastal Alabama Beach Monitoring)
channels.legal_basis: BEACH Act of 2000 (33 U.S.C. 1346): a state beach program funded under it notifies the public of exceedances of the bacteria criteria; the Coastal Alabama Beach Monitoring Program of ADEM and ADPH (statute text not quoted)
channels.note: The stations layer behind ADEM's beach monitoring map: 25 coastal stations with the last sample date, the results PDF and an advisory code (11 at every station on 2026-11-07; ADEM does not publish the codes' meaning, so any other code is read as an advisory). Read hourly by the feed. (al-adem-beach-monitoring)

channels.name: Alabama Department of Environmental Management (Coastal Alabama Beach Monitoring)
channels.legal_basis: BEACH Act of 2000 (33 U.S.C. 1346): a state beach program funded under it notifies the public of exceedances of the bacteria criteria; the Coastal Alabama Beach Monitoring Program of ADEM and ADPH (statute text not quoted)
channels.link_text: the beach monitoring map and site list
channels.note: ADEM's program page (answered 200 on 2026-11-07, the old beachMonitoring.cnt address redirects here): links to the map and the site list, each site giving its latest advisory status and results. (al-adem-beach-monitoring)

channels.name: Alabama Department of Environmental Management
channels.note: ADEM's eFile: the signed AEPACS SSO forms, searched per permit (DocType SSO; answered 200 on 2026-11-07). Each record links its permit's search; the same reports are read from ADEM's layer, so the forms are not fetched. (al-adem-efile-sso)
channels.barrier_review: the register does not say what keeps it off the web: adem's efile: the signed aepacs sso forms, searched per permit (doctype sso; answered 200 on 2026-11-07). each record li

channels.name: Alabama Department of Environmental Management
channels.note: No web form: ADEM's opt-in e-mail notice of SSO reports by county (since May 2017, at the request of Waterkeepers Alabama and the Alabama Rivers Alliance). Sign-up only; the same reports are on ADEM's map and layer. Voluntary. (al-adem-sso-email)

channels.name: Alabama Department of Environmental Management
channels.note: ADEM's public SSO map and the two layers behind it: every SSO report filed through AEPACS since 2012 (14,758 on 2026-11-07), posted within minutes of filing, with the point, start and stop, volume, receiving water and permittee; the map shows ongoing reports and those that stopped in the last 10 days. No law requires ADEM to post them: ADEM began the map after the 2017 petition. Read hourly by the feed. (al-adem-sso-history, al-adem-sso-map-live)

channels.name: Alabama Department of Public Health
channels.legal_basis: BEACH Act of 2000 (33 U.S.C. 1346): a state beach program funded under it notifies the public of exceedances of the bacteria criteria; the Coastal Alabama Beach Monitoring Program of ADEM and ADPH (statute text not quoted)
channels.note: ADPH's beach monitoring page (answered 200 on 2026-11-07). ADPH issues the coastal swim advisories as news releases (Wolf Bay at Orange Beach Waterfront Park, issued July 2026 and lifted September 2026, as the press reported) and lifts them when enterococci fall below 104 per 100 mL. Watched for changes; the advisory state itself is read from ADEM's map layer. (al-adem-beach-monitoring)

Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)
channels.note: No web form: the rule requires the permittee to report a notifiable overflow to the public as soon as possible but sets no channel or content, so no public page of the operator's is required; the operator's own pages were not searched one by one. The 2017 petition asking for a minimum standard was not adopted.

channels.name: City of LaFayette

channels.note: City of LaFayette reports each notifiable sanitary sewer overflow to ADEM within 24 hours and files the 5-day follow-up through AEPACS; ADEM posts the report on its SSO map and layer within minutes, read by the al-adem-sso-history feed. Its permits appear on ADEM's layer.

channels.name: City of Robertsdale
channels.legal_basis: Ala. Admin. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)

Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)
channels.note: No web form: the rule requires the permittee to report a notifiable overflow to the public as soon as possible but sets no channel or content, so no public page of the operator's is required; the operator's own pages were not searched one by one. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)
channels.note: No web form: the rule requires the permittee to report a notifiable overflow to the public as soon as possible but sets no channel or content, so no public page of the operator's is required; the operator's own pages were not searched one by one. The 2017 petition asking for a minimum standard was not adopted.

channels.name: Town of Crossville
channels.legal_basis: ADEM AEPACS NPDES SSO Event Reporting Form v1.5: "Immediate notification shall be provided within 24 hours of becoming aware of the event. ... The follow-up report shall be submitted within five days"; Ala. Admin. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.; NPDES permit AL0061549
channels.note: Town of Crossville reports each notifiable sanitary sewer overflow to ADEM within 24 hours and files the 5-day follow-up through AEPACS; ADEM posts the report on its SSO map and layer within minutes, read by the al-adem-sso-history feed. channels.note: Water Works and Sewer Board of the City of Wetumpka reports each notifiable sanitary sewer overflow to ADEM within 24 hours and files the 5-day follow-up through AEPACS; ADEM posts the report on its SSO map and layer within minutes, read by the al-adem-sso-history feed. Its permits appear on ADEM's layer.

channels.name: Water Works and Sewer Board of the City of Wetumpka
channels.legal_basis: Ala. Admin. Code r. 335-6-6-.12(l)6.(v): "The permittee shall report to the Director, the public, the county health department, and any other affected entity such as public water systems, as soon as possible upon becoming aware of any notifiable sanitary sewer overflow" (a notifiable SSO, r. 335-6-6-.02(hh): one that reaches a surface water of the State or may imminently and substantially endanger human health)
channels.note: No web form: the rule requires the permittee to report a notifiable overflow to the public as soon as possible but sets no channel or content, so no public page of the operator's is required; the operator's own pages were not searched one by one. The 2017 petition asking for a minimum standard was not adopted.
